title: Microsoft Purview: delete inactive OneDrives and mailboxes for departed users (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: Hold: turning off the priority cleanup tenant switch prevents new policies but does not stop existing policies from deleting content. The briefing also labels the new capability's licensing as included without establishing an entitlement, and incorrectly says the roadmap does not identify the users or accounts in scope.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Retention settings can continue to retain a departed user's OneDrive files.
claims.quote: If a user leaves your organization, any files that are subject to a retention policy or has a retention label will remain subject to the retention settings for the duration of the retention period specified in the policy or label.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A user's OneDrive site cannot be deleted while Preservation Hold library items have an unexpired retention period.
claims.quote: When one or more items in a Preservation Hold library have an unexpired retention period, the OneDrive site for the user can't be deleted.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An inactive mailbox can be permanently deleted by removing all its holds.
claims.quote: When you no longer need to keep the contents of an inactive mailbox, you can permanently delete the mailbox by removing all holds on it.

claims.claim: After the final hold is removed, an inactive mailbox is permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period.
claims.quote: Be aware that if you remove the final hold from an inactive mailbox the mailbox will be permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period expires.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be recovered after permanent deletion.
claims.quote: After the inactive mailbox is permanently deleted, it can't be recovered.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Managing priority cleanup and its tenant switch requires the Priority Cleanup Admin role.
claims.quote: you must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. For SharePoint and OneDrive, this role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, and enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires another person's approval in addition to the policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup for SharePoint and OneDrive must initially run in simulation mode.
claims.quote: Running the policy in simulation mode is required to initially set up priority cleanup for SharePoint and OneDrive locations.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires auditing enabled at least one day before the first policy runs.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: The priority cleanup tenant switch applies to Exchange as well as SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for SharePoint and OneDrive as well as for Exchange. Priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.
claims.fix: Add to controls[0].note: 'Exchange priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and is subject to change.' The cited Exchange page explicitly flags preview.

claims.claim: The tenant creation switch is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings. From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API equivalent of the priority cleanup tenant switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'priority cleanup tenant enable disable configuration PowerShell Set PriorityCleanup API'; read tenant-switch sections of priority-cleanup-onedrive-sharepoint and priority-cleanup-exchange, plus New-RetentionCompliancePolicy and Set-ComplianceTag references. No tenant-switch operation.

claims.claim: The priority cleanup creation route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.fix: The route correctly opens the wizard but stops early. For the documented static OneDrive route, extend it to 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup > Choose the type of priority cleanup > Static > Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive > Tell us what you're looking for > Choose when content should be deleted > Assign who'll approve what gets deleted > Choose the policy mode > simulation mode'. Keep query, locations, deletion settings and approver values as wizard inputs rather than invented labels.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell can create a priority cleanup policy using New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the retention policy. The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the row's whole-location, older-location inactive mailbox retention-policy hold exclusion.
claims.quote: Searched: 'delete inactive mailbox remove retention policy hold admin portal UI ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds'; read delete-an-inactive-mailbox and inactive-mailboxes-in-office-365. The row's static whole-location procedure is PowerShell; adaptive-scope UI is a different procedure.

claims.claim: Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds excludes the mailbox from whole-location retention policies using older retention locations.
claims.quote: Static scope: How to remove an inactive mailbox from a retention policy that's configured for the entire location; For retention policies that use the older retention locations: Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be removed from a retention policy with Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: You won't be able to remove an inactive mailbox if the retention policy has Preservation Lock applied.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Auditing is enabled at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on unified auditing.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: PriorityCleanupFileRecycled is an audit operation for deletion of SharePoint or OneDrive items by priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Operation name of PriorityCleanupFileRecycled: The deletion of an item in SharePoint or OneDrive by priority cleanup.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Turning off priority cleanup at tenant level turns it off for Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function; Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted; Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence after the controls table with: 'Turning off the tenant priority cleanup control prevents creation of new policies for Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive; existing policies continue to function and can be deleted, but cannot be modified.' Replace the At rollout bullet with: 'Decide whether to prevent creation of new priority cleanup policies at tenant level if your regulations require it; existing policies continue to function when this switch is off.'

claims.claim: Learn says priority cleanup can override Preservation Lock when retention settings are delete-only.
claims.quote: the deletion from priority cleanup can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock when the retention settings are for delete-only; Limitations: These items are not actually in scope for priority cleanup outside simulation mode.
claims.fix: Remove the clause 'priority cleanup can override Preservation Lock when retention settings are delete-only, and that'. The same page's Limitations section says preservation-locked items with delete-only retention settings are not actually in scope outside simulation, conflicting with its introduction and comparison table.

claims.claim: Removing holds from an inactive mailbox needs Exchange Online PowerShell, with commands depending on the hold type.
claims.quote: You must use Exchange Online PowerShell to remove holds from an inactive mailbox. You can't use the Exchange admin center (EAC), or the Microsoft Purview portal for these procedures.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'For the static-scope retention-policy exclusions shown here, use the PowerShell command documented for the policy's retention location.' The separately read https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/inactive-mailboxes-in-office-365#inactive-mailboxes-and-microsoft-365-retention also documents removal by configuring an adaptive scope to exclude the mailbox, rather than PowerShell.
